solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Union leader leaving well-liked part of London

indicators.note: leaving says a letter departs from the word for well-liked

parts.note: someone well-liked is popular

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trade union boss quits a fashionable district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' is U, and 'leaving' takes it out of POPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a district in the East End of London, in Tower Hamlets.

clue.text: Film ultimately about ancient person in northern Britain

parts.note: pic is informal for a film or picture

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A documentary about an early inhabitant of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were a people living in what is now Scotland in late antiquity and the early Middle Ages.

clue.text: Position of soft, delicate fabric

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
lace is a fine openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Reads like a fashion note on where a soft, delicate fabric is positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A place and a position are synonyms for a spot or location.

clue.text: Weak point of a cool fish she consumed

parts.note: to chill is to cool

indicators.note: consumed means eaten, so the fish takes the word she inside it

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A cold fish that a woman ate turns out to be someone's undoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' is a verb here, and 'consumed' signals containment, not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was vulnerable only in his heel, so the phrase names a fatal vulnerability.

clue.text: Old vicar returning deliveries

indicators.note: returning means the word for vicar is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman brings back what was delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries, by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over is made up of six deliveries, so the plural noun names the set.

clue.text: Curtain belonging to primeval ancestors?

indicators.note: belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A curtain that supposedly once belonged to our earliest forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A valance is a short curtain or drapery hung along the top of a window or bed frame.

clue.text: Embarrassed leftie looked in direction of …

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
to face something is to look towards it

explanation.surface: A socialist looks towards something and is mortified, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, their cheeks turning crimson.

clue.text: … bouquet delivered by post, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear signals a word that sounds the same as the one described

parts.note: a letter delivered by post has been sent

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a bunch of flowers arrives in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like flowers, but here it is the aroma of a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic aroma or smell.

clue.text: Oddly want learned judge initially having hollow look

indicators.note: oddly says these letters are arranged in a strange new way
initially points to the first letter of the word that precedes it

explanation.surface: A curious picture of a gaunt, scholarly judge in need of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges WANTLEARNED plus J, the first letter of 'judge', given by 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, thin jaw gives a gaunt face with sunken cheeks.

clue.text: Dance club held annually at first, three times

indicators.note: three times says the picked letters are written out thrice
at first points to the initial letters of the words before it

parts.note: the initials of club, held and annually again, the third copy that three times calls for

explanation.surface: A dance society meets yearly, and three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials C, H, A; 'three times' writes CHA out thrice, the third copy shown here as a bare piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Young chap in Vladivostok

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the city name that follows

explanation.surface: A young man located in the Russian port city.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lad is everyday, especially British, informal speech for a boy or youth.

clue.text: Boot I set by a big tree

parts.note: a wellington is a waterproof rubber boot

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a boot beside a large tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellingtonia is a name for the giant sequoia, a huge redwood.

clue.text: Two portions of meat — and be quick about it!

indicators.note: two says the word for a cut of meat is written twice

parts.note: a chop is a portion of meat on the bone

explanation.surface: A cook orders two cutlets and tells the butcher to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation meaning hurry up, taken from pidgin English.

clue.text: One who stops to get item of equestrian tack

definitions.meaning: someone who brings things to a standstill
a rope or strap fitted round a horse's head for leading it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who halts and a head harness for horses.

clue.text: Merciful Russian revolutionary receiving English on time

indicators.note: receiving means the revolutionary takes another letter inside him

parts.note: Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917

explanation.surface: A Russian revolutionary welcomes an Englishman punctually and shows clemency.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient person is forgiving and not harsh in judgment.

clue.text: Band going to wall in very cold weather, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a freeze is a spell of icy weather

explanation.surface: Musicians heading for a wall in icy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a decorative strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a horizontal decorative strip along the upper part of a wall.

clue.text: Financial backer a new member put up

indicators.note: put up, in a down entry, raises the word for limb so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: An investor proposes a new member for the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' is a limb here, not someone joining a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is an investor who backs a theatrical production or start-up.

clue.text: Drink with girl creating puppet show

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink
with means together with, and
Judy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone sharing a drink with a girlfriend puts on entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British seaside puppet show of a quarrelsome couple.

clue.text: Direct vehicle right into seedy bar

indicators.note: into says one letter is put inside the word for a low bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

explanation.surface: Steering a car straight into a shabby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to steer and control a car.

clue.text: Man, possibly, lives on borders of lake

parts.note: lives means is, exists

indicators.note: borders of points to the outer letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A man perhaps lives on the shores of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Ambassador carrying round garden tool

indicators.note: carrying means the diplomat holds the circle inside

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A diplomat lugging around a gardening implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled implement used for weeding.

clue.text: I weed less clumsily, seeing Alpine plant

indicators.note: clumsily says the letters before it are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An awkward gardener weeds less and finds a mountain flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white-flowered plant of the European mountains.

clue.text: Way to caress husband

parts.note: to pat is to stroke gently

explanation.surface: A method for showing affection to one's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or track to follow.

clue.text: Stick poster, for example, in this place

parts.note: a poster is one kind of advertisement, or ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Telling someone to put a poster up on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fixed to a surface.
